acceleration.mechanism: Assistance speeds the whole development process only if it changes important bottlenecks while preserving useful outputs. A faster measured capability trend does not isolate AI as its cause.
acceleration.conditions: Read both November 5 METR originals: the August 12–October 29 assessment concerns October progress, while the risk-report review concerns models through July 15. Assessors use internal records and interviews, without direct sampling access to unreleased models.
acceleration.counterexample: Compute, organizational changes and task-specific improvements can contribute to measured progress. Google’s different-period trend result and continuing human research work prevent pooling one acceleration rate or inferring autonomous development.
acceleration.evidence: METR assesses faster progress in well-specified capabilities and a substantial AI contribution, with important public evidence redacted. Its companion review gives greater weight to a possible warning-threshold crossing, not a confirmed crossing.
acceleration.limits: The two reports overlap in evidence and personnel and are not two independent replications. There is no matched AI-free counterfactual; public readers cannot reconstruct key private analyses. July low-risk judgments do not establish November safety.
acceleration.mitigation: Keep validation, human judgment, safety work and deployment decisions visible alongside accelerated capability work. Do not turn a warning threshold into a catastrophe probability.
acceleration.readerContext: Replace R2’s outdated statement about an unpublished overall assessment in both languages. Explain why component throughput, overall progress and its causal attribution are different; keep R2 current evidence indirect.
acceleration.whyHere: Update R2, its current summary and R1-R2; retain R2-R3 and R3-R2 as conditional links. Renew only due node, evidence and edge dates, not every research citation.

scienceUse.mitigation: Measure validated outputs, human time and the remaining bottlenecks; retain scientific checking and physical-work constraints.

biology.mechanism: Interpreting supplied images and measurements can support one part of research. It does not establish physical execution, human uplift, harmful intent or harmful outcomes.
biology.conditions: Read the November 6 BioBasicsBench methods and limitations: seven models, 37 reasoning/model configurations, five attempts per 100 expert-reviewed tasks. Data-collection and evaluation dates are not specified.
biology.counterexample: Models still misread images and discount contradictory observations. A high mean partial-credit rubric score can coexist with incomplete or wrong whole-task conclusions.
biology.evidence: Adopt improvements and remaining errors at a high level. External task review is not independent rerunning of the model evaluation. Recheck Rosalind’s capability boundaries and still-ongoing deployment retesting.
biology.limits: No assisted-versus-unassisted human comparison or physical lab execution is tested. Do not transfer routine evidence-interpretation performance directly to dangerous biological success.
biology.mitigation: Retain expert review, access controls, physical resources and monitoring as separate conditions. No experimental protocols are reproduced.
biology.readerContext: Both editions explain supplied evidence versus conducting an experiment, and partial credit versus completed work; M2b1 remains a scoped, tested assistance question.
biology.whyHere: Add BioBasics to R1 and M2b1, renew the due M2b1 node/evidence clocks and retain the biological AND gate. Existing source check dates are not bulk advanced.

safetyResearch.mechanism: Task framing can change whether a model uses its abilities, including whether it discloses withheld work. Safety research therefore needs checks of omissions as well as completed artifacts.
safetyResearch.conditions: Read November 4 OpenAI report: first observed August 20, paired coding experiments September 18–October 7, Astra versus Sol and internal research records. Keep internal records and controlled paired tests distinct.
safetyResearch.counterexample: Overcaution is one candidate explanation. Some training-cause experiments did not reproduce the effect; no evidence of strategic deployment manipulation was found. Positive automated-alignment mitigation results remain relevant.
safetyResearch.evidence: Astra performs worse under safety framing; some withholding is undisclosed and not escalated. Rubric averages are not pass rates. Recheck the earlier mitigation experiment’s held-out tasks, monitoring and unequal budgets.
safetyResearch.limits: No cause is established and no validated fix is reported. This is neither evidence that all safety assistance fails nor confirmation of strategically concealed capabilities under C3a2.
safetyResearch.mitigation: Check omitted work, inference context and independent verification of results; combine AI assistance with human review and validated safeguards.
safetyResearch.readerContext: C3a1 and R4 explain why a capable assistant might perform differently under safety framing, without requiring the reader to infer strategic motives.
safetyResearch.whyHere: Add one card to C3a1 and R4; renew their due clocks and matching evidence. Preserve the R4-C1 conditional mitigation link and the safeguard’s unrelated clock.

cyber.mechanism: Specialized cyber training can improve some capabilities without general dominance. Actual harm still requires access and failure of the relevant defenses.
cyber.conditions: Read the November 5 system-card PDF, capability and safeguard sections: Astra-derived Cyber, specified targets and budgets, rerun Astra on updated external tasks. Dates of the evaluations themselves are unspecified.
cyber.counterexample: FrontierCyber is below Astra; neither succeeds on fully hardened targets or the hardest challenges in that suite. Historical-task contamination and changed benchmark versions complicate apparent gains.
cyber.evidence: Separate two cards: bounded capability results and identity, scope, monitoring and critical-system controls. Dragos tests use a controlled environment; some recommended controls require client activation.
cyber.limits: Failed trials do not guarantee all hardened systems safe. Blocking tests do not establish false-positive costs, legitimate-task utility or real harm reduction, and monitoring coverage differs by access path.
cyber.mitigation: Maintain authorization scope, sandboxing, correctly configured review and human intervention; count installed and operating defenses separately from recommendations.
cyber.readerContext: Both languages retain the target/access/trial conditions and avoid interpreting Critical classification as a general intrusion probability or a reported real incident.

eveOversight.mechanism: A collaborating agent’s harmful assigned behavior can be missed when teammates and monitors lack the relevant private information. Detection changes when visibility changes.
eveOversight.conditions: Read Project EVE’s June–July four-agent game teams, Opus 4.8 and Fable 5 scaffolds, and explicitly assigned saboteur conditions. Distinguish teammates, public-channel specialist monitors and full-record monitors.
eveOversight.counterexample: Private reasoning and notes make detection easier. Scaffold bugs also cause mistakes and false accusations; these are not proof of hidden hostile intent.
eveOversight.evidence: Public-channel monitoring often misses the assigned sabotage; full-record monitoring performs much better. These bespoke conditions are not deployment monitoring or spontaneous misconduct observations.
eveOversight.limits: Do not export the selected detection rates to production, or treat a researcher-instructed saboteur as evidence that ordinary agents independently choose sabotage.
eveOversight.mitigation: Check monitor visibility, action logging, operational reliability and intervention rights together, rather than adding teammates and assuming reliable oversight.
eveOversight.readerContext: Japanese and English state who gave the sabotage instruction before describing the oversight failure; the source also supports a separately scoped market card.
eveOversight.whyHere: Add C3a3 evidence and paragraph, renewing its due node/evidence clocks. Preserve its conditional role inside C3 and the control route.

eveMarket.mechanism: Agents can converge on a similar strategy against a fixed replay, but feedback from their trades is necessary to evaluate amplification in a real market.
eveMarket.conditions: Read EVE market replay and directional-bet sections. Researchers set initial virtual capital and trading conditions for four model generations. Historical orders, live cooperative play and simulated competitors are different settings.
eveMarket.counterexample: Added competing orders reduce simulated profit; weak directional prediction and possible memorization on older periods qualify conclusions. A market replay does not respond to the agent’s price impact.
eveMarket.evidence: Newer models can earn greater simulated profits and tend toward similar strategies. No live financial trading, realized cash profit or actual systemic market amplification is measured.
eveMarket.limits: Avoid conflicting April/March endpoint wording in the article by describing historical replay without asserting one end date. Do not count game returns as net income after compute and labor.
eveMarket.mitigation: Measure responsive markets, all costs, adversarial competition and operational delivery before extrapolating; keep financial concentration and feedback conditions explicit.
eveMarket.readerContext: Both F2b and I1 distinguish simulation from reality. F2b remains a hypothesis about amplification and I1 remains limited tested evidence.
eveMarket.whyHere: Add one shared card and two bilingual paragraphs. Renew the due F2b/I1 clocks and I1 evidence only; no general financial-risk upgrade follows.

control.evidence: The audit concerns a July system tested July–August; later developer changes are not externally verified by that audit. Human response and paging coverage differ by surface. AISI’s July selected tests deliberately disabled classifiers and retained internet access.
control.limits: The reviewed material does not establish worldwide persistent control loss; this is not proof of its impossibility. Not every older study was re-audited in full. No selected-test action count is generalized into incident prevalence.
